lanes.title: Military conscience, ORA and independent legal advice
lanes.question: Does the bounded public recheck establish an implemented ORA conscience protection or post-realignment independent JAG protective outcome?

sources.title: Establishment of the Office of Religious Affairs

sources.access_result: Official PDF open returned 403 Forbidden. No new document body obtained.
sources.summary: Access recheck only; substantive clauses continue to reference retained O01.
limitations: Original-government-byte identity and current implementation remain unverified.
A blocked URL does not demonstrate withdrawal or nonimplementation.

sources.title: Hegseth Calls for Assessment, Alignment of DOW Legal Functions, Operations
sources.access_result: Official indexed text available; direct article open returned 403 Forbidden.
sources.summary: Indexed announcement describes an allocation review and states a need for independent operational legal advice. It does not report a completed independent-advice outcome.
limitations: Search excerpt is not a full retrieved article.
The later implementation and individual protection questions remain unresolved.

findings.claim: The retained ORA direction changes the Chaplains Board reporting path and includes noncompulsion protections. This cycle did not verify an operative charter, assessment-to-career rule or completed conscience remedy.
findings.basis: Historical formal direction remains documented; the queried implementation/protection outcome is unverified in this bounded check.

findings.claim: The March legal-review announcement can be reconfirmed through official indexed text; no completed JAG interference/advice disposition was obtained.
findings.basis: Announced reallocation and preservation language do not measure actual independent advice or remedy.

counterevidence: O01 retains protection for any faith or no faith and forbids compelled participation; ORA’s 60-/90-day planning milestones were still future on November4.
J03’s enacted notice/qualified-advice provisions and J15’s statutory-independence clause remain formal counterconstraints. They do not establish operational success.
The command-assessment development described in B05 predates ORA; chronology does not prove an ORA career-selection mechanism.
unknowns: Actual Board reporting practice and current implementing charter.
ORA assessment fields, identifiable-data access, consent/refusal handling and personnel use.
A substantiated conscience/appeal outcome or post-realignment JAG advice/interference disposition.
working_buffers: Formal noncompulsion, qualified legal advice and review routes remain documented possibilities; usable access and successful remedies are unverified.
lanes.next_test: Inspect one public anonymized ORA-linked conscience/accommodation disposition that records the request, access to review, decision and consequences; preserve UNKNOWN if none is available.
lanes.stop_reason: Allocated search budget exhausted and two official direct opens blocked; no inference drawn from non-retrieval.
lanes.authorship_limits: Fresh bounded search and access checks by cycle15_institutions; no service-level audit, legal adjudication or independent replication of the retained memorandum.

lanes.title: Camp East Montana TB safeguards and correction
lanes.question: Does a dated post-April18,2026 public medical reinspection or closure record verify TB intake-testing and notification corrections?

sources.title: Immigration Detention: Waste and Performance Issues at Camp East Montana Provide Valuable Lessons for Future Facilities
sources.access_result: Product page and all four recommendation/status rows returned as extracted text.
sources.summary: All four recommendations remain Open on the inspected page. DHS pricing work and Army lessons-learned milestones remain visible; the latter targets December 30, 2026.
limitations: Same report/status family as C01 and the October14 receipt, not independent medical evidence.
No raw HTTP receipt or byte-equivalence check against October14 was obtained.
Status notes have their own May/August dates; retrieval is not a new facility observation.

sources.title: ERO El Paso Camp East Montana — Inspection 2026-001-098
sources.publisher: ICE Office of Professional Responsibility / Office of Detention Oversight; public mirror hosted by KVIA
sources.access_result: 15-page PDF extracted; medical-care findings on printed pages11–12 and detainee-relations passage on printed page6 inspected.
sources.summary: ODO identifies one symptomatic person lacking required isolation and ICE/ERO notification (MC-20/21/67). This is newly inspected historical source material underlying GAO’s account.
limitations: Not a post-April18 reinspection or correction-verification record.
Government-original bytes and mirror completeness were not compared.
Extracted text, not a raw HTTP receipt; redactions/layout limit other findings.
Reusing the inspection beneath GAO adds source proximity, not an independent inspection.
sources.date_note: Inspection dates are printed on the cover; original publication date unknown. The mirror URL month is not adopted as publication date.

findings.claim: The four Open recommendation statuses and dated agency plans remain visible. They establish neither that no corrective work occurred nor that TB protections now work.
findings.basis: Fresh reading of the same GAO status surface; no status transition established.

findings.claim: The mirrored February ODO report directly supports the historical notification/isolation deficiencies. Its inspection precedes the April18 contract transition.
findings.basis: New source-level inspection of an old event, not a new failure or independent corroborating inspection.

findings.claim: Post-transition TB compliance and a protective result remain UNKNOWN in this check.
findings.basis: Neither retrieved document supplies the required post-April18 sampled verification; records elsewhere may exist.

counterevidence: ODO reports 49 voluntary interviews, generally favorable service responses, and a dietitian menu review. These narrow observations cannot establish TB protection.
The retained GAO baseline includes partial physical improvements and contractor-reported corrective plans; contract replacement is distinct from verified remedy.
unknowns: Sampled post-April18 intake testing and required notification compliance.
Correction closure date, verification method and sustained protective result.
Current safely usable capacity and replacement-contract compliance.
working_buffers: Inspection and discrepancy-report channels documented the historical failures; monitoring activity itself is not proof that they remedied them.
lanes.next_test: Obtain one dated final post-April18 medical reinspection or corrective-action closure record naming TB testing/notification, sampled compliance and the verifier. The existing FOIA draft remains unsent.
lanes.stop_reason: One fresh GAO status page and one historical underlying inspection inspected; the specified current correction outcome is not established.
lanes.authorship_limits: No facility visit, clinical record review, raw government receipt for the mirrored inspection, or independent medical verification.
